metadata.case_name: CHUNG LAI HA v. CHING MEI YEE

plaintiff.occupation_before: Superintendent of Posts (manager of the Sheung Wan Post Office)

injuries.description: multiple contusions and abrasion, bruise and soft tissue injury on her face, neck and chest wall
source: Physical examination of the plaintiff after the Incident showed multiple contusions and abrasion, bruise and soft tissue injury on her face, neck and chest wall. No other physical injuries were found.
On her last follow-up on 31 July 2009, she was diagnosed to have suffered post traumatic stress disorder ("PTSD").
Dr Yu also diagnosed the plaintiff having PTSD. He was of the opinion that the development of PTSD subsequent to the Incident was entirely attributable to the Incident.

manifestations.description: abrasion and scratch mark in the face
bruises in both arms and in chest
intense fear and a strong sense of her life being in danger; suspicion of assailants
loss of interest in travelling and participating in other activities

treatments_received.treatment: Accident & Emergency treatment at Queen Mary Hospital (QM Hospital)
source: After the Incident, the plaintiff was sent to the Accident & Emergency Department (the “A&E”) of the Queen Mary Hospital (the “QM Hospital”) for medical treatment. She was diagnosed to have suffered multiple contusions.

treatments_received.treatment: Consultation with Dr Danny PK Ma (9 July 2009)
source: The plaintiff consulted Dr Danny PK Ma (“Dr Ma”) on 9 July 2009. Physical examination showed that she had multiple abrasion, bruise and soft tissue injury.

treatments_received.treatment: Examination at Tseung Kwan O Hospital (10 July 2009) confirming injuries on face and neck and contusion of chest wall
source: She was further examined at the Tseung Kwan O Hospital (the “TKO Hospital”) on 10 July 2009 which confirmed the findings of injury on her face and neck and contusion of chest wall.

treatments_received.treatment: Psychiatric outpatient treatment at United Christian Hospital (UC Hospital) and TKO Hospital
source: She was referred to the Casualty Department of the United Christian Hospital (the “UC Hospital”) on 13 July 2009. The plaintiff complained of emotional instability after the Incident.

In her follow-up visits on 12 August 2009 and 9 September 2009 at the UC Hospital, the plaintiff reported that she remained insomniac and kept ruminating on the Incident despite medications. Her level of anxiety remained static and she had nightmares about the Incident.

treatments_received.treatment: Antidepressant medication prescribed by Dr Peter WT Yu from 30 September 2009 until November 2010
source: Dr Yu first examined the plaintiff on 30 September 2009 when the plaintiff consulted him for treatment. He prescribed an antidepressant to the plaintiff until November 2010 and continued to offer counseling to her.

treatments_received.treatment: Counseling by Dr Peter WT Yu (ongoing sessions)
source: Dr Yu first examined the plaintiff on 30 September 2009 when the plaintiff consulted him for treatment. He prescribed an antidepressant to the plaintiff until November 2010 and continued to offer counseling to her.

Dr Yu in his report stated that he expected the plaintiff to continue with her current treatment for at least three years and he offered counseling to the plaintiff at 12 weeks interval at the charge of $600.00 each time.

treatments_future.treatment: Counseling at 12-week intervals for 3 years (estimated cost $600 per session)
source: Dr Yu in his report stated that he expected the plaintiff to continue with her current treatment for at least three years and he offered counseling to the plaintiff at 12 weeks interval at the charge of $600.00 each time.

losses.description: Prevented from continuing with or advancing further at her career to which she had devoted for more than 30 years; unable to continue working at Hongkong Post and opted for early retirement.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Lost interest in travelling and participating in other activities which she used to enjoy; before the Incident she played squash and enjoyed travelling, but after the Incident she lost interest.
Avoided interacting with friends and people in her social circle; reputation affected and embarrassment from media coverage and colleagues' remarks.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Developed intense fear about the Incident recurring, avoided the assault venue, felt unsafe at home and sold her property and moved district because the defendant knew her address.
